messages:
alex: quick signal — after landing the continuous-batcher change, we see a ~20-35% tail latency increase on long sequences when using FP8 kernels. looks like kernel selection is flipping to a fallback path for some shapes. anyone seen this pattern?

nina: saw something similar in the early rollout tests. do you have a repro trace?

alex: pasted a small profile snippet below from prod-sim run (N=12 requests, 8k max seq):
```
profile: request_42
  shape: batch=3, seq=8192, kv_slots=2048
  selected_kernel: fp8_matmul_v2
  time_per_token: 5.6ms (p50), 18.3ms (p99)
fallbacks: kernel_shape_mismatch -> int8_slow_path
memory: kv_alloc_frag=18% (slab fragmentation)
```

chris: interesting — kernel_shape_mismatch usually means the tile-fit heuristic failed and we dropped into the generic int8 kernel. that generic path is slower for very long seqs.

sam: could be the quant calibration boundaries too. if the FP8 quant params are recalculated per-batch and we hit a rare outlier, we force a conservative kernel. alex, did you run with static calibration or dynamic?

alex: static calib from last run (calib-v3). no per-batch recalib. i thought that would avoid the dynamic overhead.

nina: two quick hypotheses: 1) continuous-batcher is packing inputs into shapes that are not multiples expected by fp8 kernels (tile size 32/64), causing padding and kernel fallback; 2) KV cache slab allocator fragmentation makes certain matmul dims non-contiguous so kernel-fit fails.

chris: to test #1, try forcing the scheduler to only emit batches with shape-aligned padding (pad_to=64) and compare. for #2, dump allocator arena map at request boundary and check contiguous runs.

alex: i ran a gated test toggling pad_to. results: pad_to=64 brings p99 down ~22% for the same throughput, but avg token/sec drops ~5% due to extra padding. attached minimal logs: 
```
pad=0: p99=18.3ms, avg_tp=1200 tok/s
pad=64: p99=14.1ms, avg_tp=1140 tok/s
```

sam: that tradeoff is expected. we should measure wasted_token_rate = extra_padding / total_tokens to quantify cost. if wasted_token_rate < 10% then pad_to wins for tail latency SLOs.

nina: another angle — the fp8 kernel selector looks at "shape_vec" and allocator flags. running the selector with verbose=2 on the same run produced: 
```
selector: candidate_kernels=[fp8_matmul_v2, int8_packed, generic_fp32]
score(fp8_matmul_v2) = 0.72 (requires tile_align=32, contiguous_kv=true)
contiguous_kv=false -> penalize -> score=0.31 -> fallback
```

chris: aha — contiguous_kv=false is our smoking gun. why is the KV allocator producing discontiguous slabs? continuous batching tries to reuse small prefixes and interleave writes, might be causing fragmentation.

alex: confirmed: when continuous-batcher window > 8 concurrent inflight prefixes, allocator fragmentation metric spikes.

sam: short-term: we can (A) pin pad_to to tile size when FP8 enabled, (B) reduce continuous-batcher window or coalesce KV writes, or (C) change selector to relax the contiguous requirement for fp8 kernel (but that may hurt correctness/perf).

nina: i'd prefer B + monitoring: reduce window to 6 and enable a runtime opt 'coalesce_kv_writes=true' that groups writes at checkpoint. run A as a mitigation for canary traffic.

chris: we should also run a microbenchmark for the relaxed selector: emulate non-contiguous kv but force fp8 kernel with memcpy to contiguous buffer and measure overhead. might be cheaper than padding.

alex: ran that microbench — copying into contiguous temp buffer adds ~0.4ms per matmul for 8k seqs, which is less than the fallback penalty. so selector could adaptively use copy-on-fly when fragmentation small.

perf-bot: perf-alert: CI perf regression detected on fp8 rollout branch: p99 increased 28% on long-seq suite. ticket: PERF-4292

sam: ok action list: 1) alex -> create canary with pad_to=32/64 and monitor wasted_token_rate (deploy today) 2) nina -> reduce continuous-batcher window to 6 and enable coalesce_kv_writes for canary (test infra) 3) chris -> implement selector fallback option copy-on-fly prototype and run microbench (next 48h) 4) perf -> add telemetry for kv_contiguous_ratio and tile_alignment_miss.

alex: will open change PR for pad_to canary and link PERF-4292. also attaching short repro script for local dev.

nina: i'll coordinate canary rollout and add alert thresholds.

chris: i can take the selector prototype. if copy-on-fly helps we can gate it behind an experiment flag and enable only for long-seq paths.

sam: nice. keep notes in the ticket with benchmarks and cost tradeoffs — we need to present to SRE/PM if pad-based approach increases token cost.

alex: thanks all. i'll post updates in the ticket and follow up with the canary logs when live. :thumbsup:
